headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Windsurf’s shared filesystem/clipboard meets social-auto-upload’s broad networked upload workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files and clipboard by default, and social-auto-upload consumes local files such as videos and images for upload. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if attacker-controlled text is placed in shared files or copied content. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is not safely isolated.
conditions: IF a shared file or clipboard item contains attacker-controlled instructions and Windsurf parses it as guidance
IF social-auto-upload writes or stages content that Windsurf later reads from the same workspace
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Keep the upload workspace separate from the coding workspace
Use a read-only review step before Windsurf acts on any file content
Prefix shared files with a strict machine-readable schema
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf has broad filesystem read/write plus MCP and network egress, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media files. If they share a local workspace, Windsurf can ingest those files and transmit context to third-party services, creating a realistic leakage path for account data and media without strong default isolation.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local workspace or account file
IF Windsurf sends workspace context or file contents to its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Move sensitive media and account files out of the shared workspace
Turn off MCP servers for sessions that touch account data
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents
Review and redact files before opening them in Windsurf
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; social-auto-upload also has broad network egress and session-scoped account files. Because Windsurf shares state via local filesystem across instances, concurrent edits can collide with upload state or account files, and the pair has no documented locking mechanism. Uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or account file
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while social-auto-upload is updating upload artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared files
Avoid git operations in the shared workspace
Use file locks for account and upload state
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can treat workspace content as actionable context, and social-auto-upload produces media/account artifacts that may be reused downstream. If Windsurf consumes those outputs without verification, errors in filenames, metadata, or upload parameters can cascade into incorrect uploads or broken automation. The pathway exists, but the blast radius is limited to work products rather than irreversible harm.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses social-auto-upload output as authoritative input without validation
IF upload metadata or file paths are copied into downstream commands
mitigations: Add a manual verification step before any downstream action
Validate filenames and metadata against a schema
Keep generated artifacts in a staging folder
Review diffs before execution
requires-engineering: add checksum-based handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: social-auto-upload touches account data and media, while Windsurf is a closed-source editor that can send workspace context to a model proxy and MCP servers. If regulated or personal media is opened in Windsurf, retention and residency obligations may diverge from the uploader’s handling. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal media or account data is opened in Windsurf
IF Windsurf’s model proxy or MCP servers retain prompts or file contents
mitigations: Avoid opening regulated data in Windsurf sessions
Use synthetic or redacted test assets
Check vendor retention settings before use
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows from coding workflows
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy
